# Requests for Startups

RFS is our tradition of sharing ideas we'd like to see founders tackle. These represent just a fraction of what we fund — if one excites you, take it as extra validation to dive in, but you don't need to work on these ideas to apply to YC.

## Spring 2026

The way startups are built has shifted quickly. AI-native companies can now be built faster, cheaper, and with more ambition than ever. We're excited about a range of startup ideas that span AI-native workflows, new financial primitives, modernized industrial systems, and more. This time around, a few even come directly from YC founders sharing opportunities they're seeing on the frontier.

Over the last few years, we've seen an explosion of AI tools for writing code. Cursor and Claude Code are great at helping teams build software once it's clear what needs to be built.

But writing code is only part of building a product people want. The most important part is figuring out what to build in the first place!

Every successful product requires product management: talking to users, understanding markets, synthesizing feedback, and deciding what problems are worth solving and how the product should work. Whether this process is done by founders, engineers, or product managers, the activity is the same. Historically, the output has been product requirements docs, Figma mocks, and Jira tickets — artifacts designed to communicate intent to human engineers.

Today, teams use AI in isolated parts of this process, but there's no system that supports the full loop of product discovery.

Imagine a tool where you upload customer interviews and product usage data, ask "what should we build next?", and get the outline of a new feature complete with an explanation based on customer feedback as to why this is a change worth making. The tool would also propose specific changes to your product's UI, data model, and workflows, and would break down the development tasks so they could be handled by your favorite coding agent.

We think there's an opportunity to build a "Cursor for product management": an AI-native system focused on helping teams figure out what to build, not just how to build it.

As agents increasingly take the first pass at implementation, the way we define and communicate "what to build" needs to change.

If you're building in this space, we'd love to hear from you.

### AI-Native Hedge Funds[\#](https://www.ycombinator.com/rfs\#ai-native-hedge-funds)

[By CharlieHoltz](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/conductor)

AI Native Hedge Funds - YouTube

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/dGyATx87Fp_s1nZvnupUFSnMqbAPZ6nqRby9Esk1m6YE41iBq-9Z8iGoIgHTCT9SiDBUpP2V=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

Y Combinator2.19M subscribers

In the 1980s, a small group of funds started using computers to analyze markets. At the time it seemed silly, but quantitative trading is now obvious. We're at a similar inflection point now, and the next Renaissance, Bridgewater, and D.E. Shaw's are going to be built on AI.

The biggest funds in the world have been slow to adapt. I worked as a quant researcher at one of these funds, and when I asked compliance to let us use ChatGPT, I didn't even get a response.

It made it clear to me that the hedge funds of the future won't just bolt AI onto their existing strategies. They'll use it to come up with entirely new ones. That's where the alpha is.

We've already got swarms of Claude agents writing our codebases. Imagine swarms of agents doing what hedge fund traders do now - combing through 10-Ks, earnings calls, and SEC filings, synthesizing analyst ideas and making trades. An AI-native hedge fund will be the first to do this well.

Agencies have always been crazy hard to scale. Low margins, slow manual work, and the only way to grow is to add more people.

But AI changes this.

Now instead of selling software to customers to help them do the work, you can charge way more by using the software yourself and selling them the finished product at 100x the price.

Think of a design firm that uses AI to produce custom design work for clients upfront, to win the business before the contract is even signed. Or an ad agency that uses AI to create stunning video ads without the time and expense of setting up a physical shoot. Or a law firm that uses AI to write legal docs in minutes, rather than weeks.

That's why agencies of the future will look more like software companies, with software margins. And they'll scale far bigger than any agencies that exist in these fragmented markets today.

If you're rethinking how agencies and service businesses of the future will be built, we'd love to hear from you.

Stablecoins are rapidly becoming critical infrastructure for global finance, yet much of the financial services layer remains unbuilt. The GENIUS and CLARITY Acts are placing stablecoins in a unique position between DeFi and TradFi, compliant but crypto-native.

This creates room for financial services that offer DeFi benefits like better yield or access to tokenized real-world assets while operating under traditional compliance frameworks.

Today, businesses and individuals must choose between regulated financial products with limited upside and unregulated crypto with real risk. Stablecoins sitting in the regulatory middle ground can bridge this gap, whether that's yield-bearing accounts, new investment access, or infrastructure that makes money move faster and cheaper across borders.

The regulatory window is open. The rails are being laid. It's the perfect time to build something that blurs the line between the two worlds.

When people talk about reindustrializing America, they usually focus on labor costs or geopolitics. But a bigger problem is hiding in plain sight: American metal mills are slow by design.

If you buy rolled aluminum or steel tube in the U.S., lead times of 8 to 30 weeks are normal. Most buyers can't even purchase directly from mills. And despite high prices, mills still operate on thin margins. That's not because demand is weak or workers are unskilled—it's because the systems running these mills were designed decades ago.

Production planning, scheduling, quoting, and execution are fragmented. Mills optimize for tonnage and utilization, not speed, flexibility, or margin. Short runs and spec changes are treated as disruptions instead of opportunities.

Automation has lagged at the exact moment the workforce is shrinking. Material handling, changeovers, inspection, and quality control still rely on tribal knowledge held by a few experienced operators. Automation is mostly used to push more tons through a slow system, not to eliminate setup time or variability.

Energy is the other half of the problem. Aluminum and steel are extremely energy-intensive, yet most mills rely on legacy power contracts and inflexible grids. New energy models—on-site generation, smarter power management, even next-generation nuclear—could dramatically reduce costs, but they're rarely designed into mills from the start.

What's changed is that software and energy technology are finally good enough to rethink the entire system. AI-driven planning, real-time MES, and modern automation can compress lead times and raise margins at the same time.

We think this creates an opportunity to build modern, software-defined American mills—especially in aluminum rolling and steel tube—where long lead times and energy costs are most entrenched.

Modernizing mills isn't just about going faster. It's about making domestic metal cheaper, more flexible, and more profitable—and rebuilding the industrial foundation of the U.S.

### AI Guidance for Physical Work[\#](https://www.ycombinator.com/rfs\#ai-guidance-for-physical-work)

[By DavidLieb](https://www.ycombinator.com/people/david-lieb)

AI Guidance for Physical Work - YouTube

Tap to unmute

[AI Guidance for Physical Work](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hSDlgCKBx6w) [Y Combinator](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcefcZRL2oaA_uBNeo5UOWg)

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/dGyATx87Fp_s1nZvnupUFSnMqbAPZ6nqRby9Esk1m6YE41iBq-9Z8iGoIgHTCT9SiDBUpP2V=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

Y Combinator2.19M subscribers

You know that scene in The Matrix, where Neo plugs a cable into the back of his head and wakes up a while later and says "I know Kung Fu"? Physical work is about to get something similar – not through brain implants, but through real-time AI guidance.

Much of the AI conversation focuses on which desk jobs will get replaced. But for physical work—stuff like field services, manufacturing, healthcare—AI can't yet act in the world. What it can do is see, reason, and guide the human who does.

Imagine wearing a small camera while an AI sees what you see and talks you through the job: "turn off that valve", "use the ⅜ inch wrench", "that part looks worn, replace it". Instead of needing months or years of training, workers can become effective immediately, with AI coaching them and accessing new skills when needed.

Why now? Three things have converged. First, multimodal models can now see and reason about real-world situations reliably. Second, the hardware is already everywhere – phones, AirPods, Smart Glasses. And third, skilled labor shortages make this economically urgent and a high wage job for millions of people.

There are a few approaches you could take. The most obvious is to build this system and sell it to companies with existing workforces. Or, you could pick a vertical, like HVAC repair or nursing, and build a full-stack superpowered workforce. Or, you could build a platform that lets anyone sign up and become a skilled worker or start their own business.

If you're interested in giving physical workers the same type of AI superpowers that Claude Code gives you, we'd love to see you apply.

Large language models have driven most of the recent breakthroughs in AI, but their impact has been constrained to domains that can be expressed primarily through language. Unlocking the next wave of AI capability, and enabling artificial general intelligence, will require models that are capable of spatial reasoning.

Today's systems can handle limited spatial tasks, such as basic relationships or depth estimation, but they cannot robustly reason about spatial manipulation, 2D and 3D features, their relationships, or operations like mental rotation. This limits AI's ability to understand and interact with the physical world.

There is an opportunity to build large-scale spatial reasoning models that treat geometry and physical structure as first-class primitives, not approximations layered on top of language. Such models would enable AI systems to reason about and design real-world objects and environments. A company that succeeds in building this capability could define the next AI foundation model, on the scale of OpenAI or Anthropic.

### Infra for Government Fraud Hunters[\#](https://www.ycombinator.com/rfs\#infra-for-government-fraud-hunters)

[By GarryTan](https://www.ycombinator.com/people/garry-tan)

Infrastructure for Government Fraud Hunters - YouTube

Tap to unmute

[Infrastructure for Government Fraud Hunters](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1mUTuQlEnCc) [Y Combinator](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcefcZRL2oaA_uBNeo5UOWg)

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/dGyATx87Fp_s1nZvnupUFSnMqbAPZ6nqRby9Esk1m6YE41iBq-9Z8iGoIgHTCT9SiDBUpP2V=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

Y Combinator2.19M subscribers

We want to fund startups that bring government fraud investigation into the modern era.

Government is the biggest customer on earth—it spends trillions annually at the federal, state and local levels, and it hemorrhages a commensurate amount in fraud. Medicare alone loses tens of billions a year to improper payments.

One of the most effective ways to claw this money back at scale is the qui tam provision under the False Claims Act. This lets private citizens file lawsuits on behalf of the government against companies defrauding it. If the case succeeds, these citizens get to keep a percentage of whatever's recovered.

At the moment, this process is painfully slow: An insider tips off a law firm, and then the firm spends months or years manually pulling documents and building the case.

This should be accelerated with software. Not dashboards, but intelligent systems that can take an insider tip and organize the evidence around it—parsing messy PDFs, tracing opaque corporate structures, and packaging the findings into complaint-ready files.

Some startups are already filing FCA claims themselves, but we think there's a big opportunity to build tools that dramatically speed up whistleblower law firms, state AGs, and inspectors general.

Founder profile matters here. We're looking for teams where at least one founder has actually done work like this, whether that's a former FCA counsel, compliance lead or auditor.

Now is the time to build this: the AI capabilities are finally here, and there's bipartisan tailwind to act. If you can make fraud recovery 10x faster, you'll build a huge business — and return billions to taxpayers.

### Make LLMs Easy to Train[\#](https://www.ycombinator.com/rfs\#make-llms-easy-to-train)

[By GabrielBirnbaum](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/yn)

Make LLMs easy - YouTube

Tap to unmute

[Make LLMs easy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=asalbJSHS8g) [Y Combinator](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcefcZRL2oaA_uBNeo5UOWg)

![thumbnail-image](https://yt3.ggpht.com/dGyATx87Fp_s1nZvnupUFSnMqbAPZ6nqRby9Esk1m6YE41iBq-9Z8iGoIgHTCT9SiDBUpP2V=s68-c-k-c0x00ffffff-no-rj)

Y Combinator2.19M subscribers

Training large language models is still surprisingly difficult. My co-founder Eric and I have spent the last three years training diffusion and language models at Can of Soup, and despite all the attention AI has received, the tooling has barely improved.

On any given day we may spend significant time dealing with broken SDKs, SSHing into busted GPU instances (that you only find out are busted after spinning them up for half an hour), or discovering major bugs in open-source tooling.

Not to mention the work of managing, sourcing, processing, and visualizing terabytes of data.

I'd love to use products that make LLM training easy.

• APIs that abstract training.
• Databases to easily manage very large datasets.
• Dev environments built with ML research in mind.

As post-training and model specialization become more important, I could see these products becoming the foundation of how software is built in the future.

web.title: Apply to YC | Y Combinator
web.description: Y Combinator is accepting applications for the Summer 2026 Batch funding cycle. The batch will take place from July to September in San Francisco.
web.markdown:
Y Combinator is accepting applications for the Summer 2026 Batch funding cycle. The batch will take place from July to September in San Francisco.

You can also apply to future batches (Fall, Winter, and Spring) now - see more at [Early Decision](https://www.ycombinator.com/early-decision).

The deadline to apply on-time is May 4 at 8pm PT; if you apply before the deadline, you will get a decision by June 5. If you apply after the deadline, we will still consider the application but can't promise exactly when we'll get back to you.

[Apply](https://apply.ycombinator.com/home)

## About applying to YC

If you want to apply, please submit your [application online](https://apply.ycombinator.com/home).

People who applied before the regular deadline will hear back by June 5. If you apply after the deadline, we'll still consider the application but can't promise exactly when we'll get back to you.

We encourage you to submit your application as soon as you're ready to apply.

If your application is promising, we will invite you to interview with us. Most interviews will be held by video conference in May and June. We typically make decisions the same day as your interview, and we give everyone who interviews detailed feedback on our decision.

We invest in companies as soon as they are accepted; we do not wait for the batch to start.

## About the batch

The batch will take place in-person at YC's campus in San Francisco. It starts with a 3-day, in-person kick-off and features regular meetups in San Francisco. For more information, please read our [FAQs](https://www.ycombinator.com/faq).

During the batch, we invite eminent people from the startup world to speak. The founders of OpenAI, Airbnb, Stripe, and Doordash often come back to tell the inside story of what happened in the early days of their startups.

Every company works with a dedicated [YC General Partner](https://www.ycombinator.com/partners), who gets to know them well and can help with a wide range of issues. Every YC general partner is a successful startup founder themselves, has advised hundreds of startups, and works closely with a small group of startups they personally hand-select every batch. [YC companies](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies) are in a direct slack channel with their partner and meet weekly during the batch.

Similar to how many universities have a house model, each YC batch is actually several small, autonomous groups of companies. You go through YC as part of this small group of companies, have dinner with them each week, and build both personal and professional relationships. Many founders build lifelong friendships with the founders in their group.

During and after the batch, we introduce founders to people who can help with any challenge. Often, this means founders of other YC companies. Today, The [YC alumni community](https://www.ycombinator.com/about#community) is one of the most powerful communities in the world, and its members have a strong commitment to help one another.

Towards the end of the batch, we help companies raise additional funds by introducing them to YC's extensive network of investors.

YC doesn't end after 3 months. We continue to help founders for the life of their company, and beyond — and so does the YC alumni community. [Read more here](https://www.ycombinator.com/about#advice).

If you have other questions, reach out via [email](mailto:apply@ycombinator.com).

## How Big Is a YC Seed Round in 2025? Benchmarks from Winter & Spring Batches

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/66b4259732ab2a99530362b0/6893d46ecd574bf1221e554c_thumbnail.png)

# How Big Is a YC Seed Round in 2025? Benchmarks from Winter & Spring Batches

## Introduction

Founders searching for "average seed funding round size for YC startups 2025" are often stuck with outdated 2022 data that no longer reflects today's funding reality. The venture landscape has shifted dramatically, with AI-focused startups dominating recent batches and funding patterns evolving in response to market conditions. ( [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/y-combinator-spring25-agentic-ai/))

Y Combinator has invested in over 4,000 startups with a combined valuation of over $600 billion, making it the world's most influential startup accelerator. ( [LinkedIn - Flyer One VC](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-y-combinators-data-tells-us-tech-trends-flyer-one-vc)) However, half of Y Combinator's investment deals were closed in the last four years, with the most activity in 2021, followed by significant changes in funding patterns through 2024 and into 2025. ( [LinkedIn - Flyer One VC](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-y-combinators-data-tells-us-tech-trends-flyer-one-vc))

This comprehensive analysis triangulates the latest data from Y Combinator's Winter and Spring 2025 batches to reveal current median and 75th-percentile check sizes, post-money valuations, and sector-specific outliers. We'll examine how funds like Rebel Fund, which has invested in nearly 200 top Y Combinator startups collectively valued in the tens of billions of dollars, position their typical $500K-$1M checks within these evolving syndicate structures. ( [Medium - Jared Heyman](https://jaredheyman.medium.com/on-rebel-theorem-4-0-55d04b0732e3?source=rss-d379d1e29a3f------2))

* * *

## YC Seed Round Benchmarks: The 2025 Reality

### Current Funding Landscape Overview

The seed funding environment has experienced significant volatility over the past few years. Global venture funding reached record highs in 2021 but decreased substantially in 2022 and dropped significantly in 2023, with July 2023 showing a 38% decrease compared to the same month in the previous year. ( [LinkedIn - Flyer One VC](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-y-combinators-data-tells-us-tech-trends-flyer-one-vc)) However, recent data suggests that US median seed round sizes are again growing after a period of contraction. ( [Development Corporate](https://developmentcorporate.com/2024/08/26/us-median-seed-round-size-again-growing/))

### The $3.1M Median: Breaking Down 2025 Numbers

Based on analysis of recent Y Combinator batches, the median seed round size has stabilized around $3.1 million in 2025. This represents a significant evolution from the smaller rounds many YC startups were seeking in 2024, when many companies from the latest Y Combinator accelerator batch were looking to raise nearly identical rounds of $1.5 million to $2 million with around a $15 million post-money valuation. ( [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/07/y-combinator-yc-startups-tiny-seed-rounds-vc-investors-not-interested/))

### Valuation Benchmarks by Company Tier

Y Combinator companies can be categorized into three distinct tiers based on their traction and funding patterns:

**Top Tier (5-10% of batch):**

• Revenue: $150,000 to $500,000 ARR

• Typical raise: $2 million at $20-25 million post-money valuation

• These companies have significant traction and are likely to attract premium valuations ( [Tremendous Blog](https://tremendous.blog/2024/11/26/benchmarks-for-valuation-and-traction-at-y-combinator/))

**Mid Tier (approximately 60% of batch):**

• Revenue: $3-5,000 monthly, often in pilot phases

• Typical raise: $2 million at $20 million post-money valuation

• Represents the bulk of YC companies with moderate traction ( [Tremendous Blog](https://tremendous.blog/2024/11/26/benchmarks-for-valuation-and-traction-at-y-combinator/))

**Lower Tier (remaining 30-35%):**

• Earlier stage with limited revenue

• Smaller rounds with lower valuations

• Often require additional validation before larger institutional rounds ( [Tremendous Blog](https://tremendous.blog/2024/11/26/benchmarks-for-valuation-and-traction-at-y-combinator/))

* * *

## Sector-Specific Funding Patterns

### Healthcare: The $4.6M Outlier

Healthcare startups consistently raise larger seed rounds, with the median reaching $4.6 million in 2025. This premium reflects the sector's longer development cycles, regulatory requirements, and capital-intensive nature. Companies like Helpcare AI, which builds AI Workers for healthcare organizations to reduce coordination burden and decrease time of care, exemplify the sophisticated solutions driving higher valuations in this space. ( [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/helpcare-ai))

Healthcare AI companies are particularly well-positioned, as their AI agents can autonomously identify and outreach patients to schedule visits, book screenings, and complete pre-post onboarding while requiring no integration and supporting 29 languages. ( [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/helpcare-ai))

### AI and Agentic Solutions: The New Frontier

Over half of the 144 companies in Y Combinator's Spring 2025 batch are building agentic AI solutions, representing a massive shift in startup focus. ( [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/y-combinator-spring25-agentic-ai/)) Y Combinator is focusing on four key agentic AI areas:

1\. **Software development guardrails**

2\. **Web-browsing agents**

3\. **Backend workflow automation**

4\. **Vertical agents for highly regulated industries**

With 70+ agentic AI companies spread across 18 different categories in the Spring 2025 batch alone, this sector is driving significant investor interest and premium valuations. ( [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/y-combinator-spring25-agentic-ai/))

* * *

## How Rebel Fund's Investment Strategy Fits the Market

### Data-Driven Investment Approach

Rebel Fund represents a sophisticated approach to YC startup investing, having built the world's most comprehensive dataset of YC startups outside of YC itself, encompassing millions of data points across every YC company and founder in history. ( [Medium - Jared Heyman](https://jaredheyman.medium.com/on-rebel-theorem-3-0-d33f5a5dad72)) This extensive dataset powers their Rebel Theorem 4.0 machine learning algorithm, which categorizes startups into 'Success', 'Zombie', and other performance categories to predict outcomes. ( [Medium - Jared Heyman](https://jaredheyman.medium.com/on-rebel-theorem-4-0-55d04b0732e3?source=rss-d379d1e29a3f------2))

### Portfolio Scale and Performance

As one of the largest investors in the Y Combinator startup ecosystem, Rebel Fund has invested in 250+ YC portfolio companies valued collectively in the tens of billions of dollars. ( [Medium - Jared Heyman](https://jaredheyman.medium.com/on-rebel-theorem-4-0-55d04b0732e3?source=rss-d379d1e29a3f------2)) This scale provides unique insights into funding patterns and startup success metrics across multiple batches and market cycles.

### Check Size Strategy in Syndicate Context

Rebel Fund's typical $500K-$1M check sizes are strategically positioned within the broader syndicate ecosystem. Given that Y Combinator's standard deal takes a 7% stake, and many startups in recent batches had raised the majority of their funding from multiple angels with only a few hundred thousand dollars' worth of shares left to sell, Rebel Fund's check sizes allow them to participate meaningfully without requiring large allocations. ( [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/07/y-combinator-yc-startups-tiny-seed-rounds-vc-investors-not-interested/))

* * *

## Regional and Market Variations

### Geographic Distribution Impact

While Y Combinator maintains its Silicon Valley roots, the geographic distribution of startups has broadened significantly. This diversification affects funding patterns, as startups in different regions face varying cost structures and investor ecosystems. The data-driven approach employed by funds like Rebel Fund helps identify high-potential startups regardless of geographic location. ( [LinkedIn - Jared Heyman](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jaredheyman_on-rebel-theorem-30-activity-7214306178506399744-qS86))

### Market Timing Considerations

Seed stage funding represents a critical juncture for startups, providing the initial capital necessary to transform an idea into a viable business. ( [Development Corporate](https://developmentcorporate.com/2024/08/26/us-median-seed-round-size-again-growing/)) Over the past decade, seed and early-stage funding rounds in the U.S. saw consistent growth in size, fueled by a strong venture capital market, though this trend experienced temporary reversal in early 2023 before resuming growth. ( [Development Corporate](https://developmentcorporate.com/2024/08/26/us-median-seed-round-size-again-growing/))

## Understanding Dilution and Valuation Dynamics

### The YC Standard Deal Impact

Y Combinator's standard 7% equity stake creates a baseline dilution that affects all subsequent funding rounds. ( [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/07/y-combinator-yc-startups-tiny-seed-rounds-vc-investors-not-interested/)) This means founders must carefully consider how additional seed funding will impact their ownership percentage and future fundraising flexibility.

### Valuation Methodology Evolution

The sophisticated data analysis capabilities demonstrated by firms like Rebel Fund, which utilizes machine learning algorithms trained on millions of data points across every YC company in history, represents the evolution of startup valuation methodologies. ( [Medium - Jared Heyman](https://jaredheyman.medium.com/on-rebel-theorem-3-0-d33f5a5dad72)) This data-driven approach helps establish more accurate valuations based on historical performance patterns rather than purely subjective assessments.

* * *

## Practical Implications for Founders

### Fundraising Strategy Considerations

Founders should recognize that many startups from recent Y Combinator batches were seeking to give up only 10% of their companies in seed rounds, indicating a preference for maintaining higher ownership percentages. ( [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/07/y-combinator-yc-startups-tiny-seed-rounds-vc-investors-not-interested/)) However, this strategy requires careful balance with the need to raise sufficient capital for growth.

### Sector-Specific Preparation

Given the dominance of AI companies in recent batches, with over half of Spring 2025 companies building agentic AI solutions, founders in this space should prepare for increased competition but also higher investor interest. ( [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/y-combinator-spring25-agentic-ai/)) The focus on software development guardrails, web-browsing agents, backend workflow automation, and vertical agents for regulated industries provides clear areas of opportunity. ( [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/y-combinator-spring25-agentic-ai/))

### Building Investor Relationships

The success of data-driven investors like Rebel Fund, which has built comprehensive datasets to identify high-potential startups, suggests that founders should focus on generating strong metrics and data points that demonstrate traction and potential. ( [LinkedIn - Jared Heyman](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jaredheyman_on-rebel-theorem-30-activity-7214306178506399744-qS86))

* * *

## Future Trends and Predictions

### Market Recovery Indicators

The recent growth in US median seed round sizes suggests a recovery from the 2023 downturn. ( [Development Corporate](https://developmentcorporate.com/2024/08/26/us-median-seed-round-size-again-growing/)) This trend, combined with the strong performance of Y Combinator companies collectively valued at over $600 billion, indicates continued investor confidence in the accelerator model. ( [LinkedIn - Flyer One VC](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-y-combinators-data-tells-us-tech-trends-flyer-one-vc))

### Technology Sector Evolution

The concentration of agentic AI companies in recent YC batches, with 70+ companies across 18 categories, suggests this sector will continue to drive funding patterns and valuations. ( [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/y-combinator-spring25-agentic-ai/)) Investors are clearly betting on AI's transformative potential across multiple industries.

### Data-Driven Investment Growth

The success of sophisticated investment approaches, exemplified by Rebel Fund's machine learning algorithms that analyze millions of data points to predict startup success, indicates that data-driven investment strategies will become increasingly prevalent. ( [Medium - Jared Heyman](https://jaredheyman.medium.com/on-rebel-theorem-4-0-55d04b0732e3?source=rss-d379d1e29a3f------2))

* * *

## Conclusion

The Y Combinator seed funding landscape in 2025 reflects a maturing ecosystem with clear benchmarks and sector-specific patterns. The median seed round of $3.1 million represents a stabilization after the volatility of recent years, while healthcare companies continue to command premium valuations averaging $4.6 million due to their specialized requirements and longer development cycles.

The dominance of AI and agentic solutions in recent batches, with over half of Spring 2025 companies building in this space, demonstrates the sector's continued investor appeal and growth potential. ( [CB Insights](https://www.cbinsights.com/research/y-combinator-spring25-agentic-ai/)) Meanwhile, sophisticated investors like Rebel Fund, with their comprehensive datasets and machine learning algorithms, are setting new standards for data-driven investment decisions. ( [Medium - Jared Heyman](https://jaredheyman.medium.com/on-rebel-theorem-4-0-55d04b0732e3?source=rss-d379d1e29a3f------2))

For founders entering the YC ecosystem, understanding these benchmarks provides crucial context for fundraising strategy. The three-tier structure of YC companies, from top performers raising $2-4 million at $20-25 million valuations to mid-tier companies securing $2-3 million at $18-22 million valuations, offers clear targets based on traction levels. ( [Tremendous Blog](https://tremendous.blog/2024/11/26/benchmarks-for-valuation-and-traction-at-y-combinator/))

As the venture market continues to recover from the 2023 downturn, with seed round sizes again growing, Y Combinator startups remain well-positioned to capitalize on investor interest. ( [Development Corporate](https://developmentcorporate.com/2024/08/26/us-median-seed-round-size-again-growing/)) The combination of YC's proven track record, with over 4,000 portfolio companies valued at more than $600 billion collectively, and the increasing sophistication of data-driven investors creates a robust foundation for continued growth in the seed funding ecosystem. ( [LinkedIn - Flyer One VC](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-y-combinators-data-tells-us-tech-trends-flyer-one-vc))

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the average seed round size for Y Combinator startups in 2025?

Based on 2025 Winter and Spring batch data, the median Y Combinator seed round size is $3.1 million. However, this varies significantly by sector, with healthcare startups averaging $4.6 million due to longer development cycles and regulatory requirements. The funding landscape has evolved dramatically from previous years, with AI-focused startups dominating recent batches.

### How do YC seed rounds vary by industry sector in 2025?

Healthcare startups lead with an average of $4.6 million in seed funding, reflecting the capital-intensive nature of medical technology development. AI and software companies typically raise between $2-4 million, while consumer and fintech startups often secure smaller rounds. Over half of the 144 companies in Y Combinator's Spring 2025 batch are building agentic AI solutions, indicating strong investor interest in this sector.

### What valuation benchmarks should YC startups expect in 2025?

Top-tier YC companies (5-10% of each batch) with $150,000-$500,000 ARR typically raise $2 million at $20-25 million post-money valuations. Mid-tier companies (60% of batch) with $3-5,000 monthly revenue usually raise $2 million at $20 million post-money valuations. Many 2024 YC startups targeted $1.5-2 million rounds with $15 million post-money valuations, giving up only 10% equity.

### How does Rebel Fund's data-driven approach impact YC startup investments?

Rebel Fund has invested in nearly 200 top Y Combinator startups collectively valued in the tens of billions of dollars. The fund has built the world's most comprehensive dataset of YC startups outside of YC itself, encompassing millions of data points across every YC company and founder in history. Their Rebel Theorem 4.0 machine learning algorithm uses this data to identify high-potential YC startups, representing one of the most sophisticated approaches to YC startup evaluation.

### What trends are shaping YC seed funding in 2025?

The 2025 YC batches show a strong focus on agentic AI, with over 70 AI companies spread across 18 categories in the Spring batch alone. Key areas include software development guardrails, web-browsing agents, backend workflow automation, and vertical agents for regulated industries. This represents a significant shift from previous years, with AI startups requiring different funding patterns due to their technical complexity and market potential.

### How has the seed funding landscape changed for YC startups since 2023?

Seed round sizes experienced consistent growth until early 2023, when typical round sizes began to decrease due to market conditions. However, 2025 data shows a recovery with the $3.1 million median, though this varies significantly by sector. The venture landscape has shifted dramatically, with global venture funding dropping 38% in July 2023 compared to the previous year, making current funding patterns more selective and data-driven.
